bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷六十一 吳世家第一: 楊行密
title.raw: 卷六十一 吳世家第一: 楊行密 Volume 61: Hereditary House of Wu

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 自唐失其政，天下乘時，黥髡盜販，袞冕峨巍。

translations.literal: From the time Tang lost proper governance, the realm seized the moment; tattooed convicts and bandit peddlers wore ceremonial caps and robes towering high.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tang lost hold of government, the whole world seized its chance: branded felons and traffickers in stolen goods donned court robes and caps as grand as any emperor's.

sentences.zh: 吳暨南唐，奸豪竊攘。

translations.literal: Wu and Southern Tang—villainous strongmen seized power through theft and usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu and Southern Tang alike, ruthless adventurers stole the realm for themselves.

sentences.zh: 蜀險而富，漢險而貧，貧能自強，富者先亡。

translations.literal: Shu was perilous yet wealthy; Han was perilous yet poor. Poverty could drive self-strengthening; the wealthy perished first.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was rugged and rich, Han rugged and poor; poverty could steel a state to endure, while wealth invited ruin first.

sentences.zh: 閩陋荊蹙，楚開蠻服。

translations.literal: Min was crude and cramped; Jing was constrained; Chu opened the land and brought the barbarians to submission.
translations.idiomatic: Min was mean and hemmed in, Jing pressed tight on every side, while Chu opened the frontier and brought the southern tribes to heel.

sentences.zh: 剝剽弗堪，吳越其尤。

translations.literal: Extortion and plunder were unbearable; Wu and Yue were worst of all.
translations.idiomatic: Extortion and plunder grew unbearable, and none suffered more than Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 牢牲視人，嶺皞遭劉。

translations.literal: Penned sacrificial beasts looked upon men; Ling Hao fell victim to Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Men were treated like livestock bound for slaughter, and Ling Hao was brought low by the Liu clan of the south.

sentences.zh: 百年之間，並起爭雄，山川亦絕，風氣不通。

translations.literal: Within a hundred years, rivals rose together vying for supremacy; mountains and rivers were cut off, and customs could not flow between regions.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single century they all rose at once to vie for supremacy, until mountains and rivers were cut off from one another and no common culture could pass between them.

sentences.zh: 語曰：清風興，群陰伏；

translations.literal: The saying goes: when the clear wind rises, all yin shades subside;
translations.idiomatic: As the saying has it: when the clear wind rises, every shadow retreats;

sentences.zh: 日月出，爝火息。

translations.literal: when sun and moon emerge, torch-flame dies.
translations.idiomatic: when sun and moon appear, the torch's flicker goes out.

sentences.zh: 故真人作而天下同。

translations.literal: Therefore when the true lord appears, the realm becomes one.
translations.idiomatic: And so when the true sovereign arises, the realm is united as one.

sentences.zh: 作《十國世家》。

translations.literal: I composed the 《Hereditary Houses of the Ten Kingdoms》.
translations.idiomatic: Hence I wrote the 《Hereditary Houses of the Ten Kingdoms》.

sentences.zh: 楊行密，字化源，廬州合淝人也。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi, courtesy name Huayuan, was a native of Hefei in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi, whose courtesy name was Huayuan, came from Hefei in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 為人長大有力，能手舉百斤。

translations.literal: As a man he was tall and powerful, able to lift a hundred jin with his hands.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and powerfully built and could lift a hundred jin in his hands.

sentences.zh: 唐乾符中，江、淮群盜起，行密以為盜見獲，刺史鄭棨奇其狀貌，釋縛縱之。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era of Tang, bandits rose throughout the Jianghuai region. Xingmi was captured as a bandit; Prefect Zheng Qi marveled at his appearance, untied his bonds, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu reign of Tang, brigands rose all along the Yangzi and Huai. Xingmi was seized as one of them, but Prefect Zheng Qi was struck by his bearing, loosed his bonds, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 後應募為州兵，戍朔方，遷隊長。

translations.literal: Later he enlisted as a prefectural soldier, garrisoned Shuofang, and was promoted to squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: He later enlisted in the prefectural militia, served on garrison duty in Shuofang, and rose to squad leader.

sentences.zh: 歲滿戍還，而軍吏惡之，復使出戍。

translations.literal: When his term of garrison duty ended and he returned, the military clerks disliked him and sent him out to garrison again.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour ended and he came home, the camp officers took a dislike to him and sent him out on garrison duty once more.

sentences.zh: 行密將行，過軍吏舍，軍吏陽為好言，問行密行何所欲。

translations.literal: As Xingmi was about to depart, he passed the military clerk's quarters. The clerk feigned friendly words and asked what Xingmi wanted on his journey.
translations.idiomatic: As Xingmi was setting out, he stopped by the clerk's quarters; the man spoke to him with feigned warmth and asked what he wanted for the road ahead.

sentences.zh: 行密奮然曰：「惟少公頭爾！

translations.literal: Xingmi said with sudden force: "Nothing but your young lordship's head!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi flared up and said, "All I want is your head!"

sentences.zh: 」即斬其首，攜之而出，因起兵為亂，自號八營都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: " He at once cut off the man's head, carried it out, then raised troops in revolt and styled himself Commander-in-Chief of the Eight Camps.
translations.idiomatic: " He struck off the man's head at once, carried it out with him, raised troops in rebellion, and styled himself Commander-in-Chief of the Eight Camps.

sentences.zh: 刺史郎幼復棄城走，行密遂據廬州。

translations.literal: Prefect Lang Youfu abandoned the city and fled; Xingmi then seized Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Lang Youfu abandoned the city and fled, and Xingmi took possession of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 中和三年，唐即拜行密廬州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhonghe, Tang at once appointed Xingmi Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhonghe, the Tang court appointed him Prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使高駢為畢師鐸所攻，駢表行密行軍司馬，行密率兵數千赴之。

translations.literal: Huainan Military Governor Gao Pian was attacked by Bi Shiduo. Pian memorialized to make Xingmi Acting Commander of the Campaign Army, and Xingmi led several thousand troops to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian, military governor of Huainan, came under attack from Bi Shiduo; Pian recommended Xingmi as acting campaign commander, and Xingmi marched to his relief with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 行至天長，師鐸已囚駢，召宣州秦彥入揚州，行密不得入，屯於蜀岡。

translations.literal: When he reached Tianchang, Shiduo had already imprisoned Pian and summoned Qin Yan of Xuanzhou into Yangzhou. Xingmi could not enter and encamped at Shugang.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Tianchang, Shiduo had already imprisoned Pian and brought Qin Yan of Xuanzhou into Yangzhou; unable to enter the city, Xingmi encamped at Shugang.

sentences.zh: 師鐸兵眾數萬擊行密，行密陽敗，棄營走，師鐸兵饑，乘勝爭入營收軍實，行密反兵擊之，師鐸大敗，單騎走入城，遂殺高駢。

translations.literal: Shiduo's army of tens of thousands attacked Xingmi. Xingmi feigned defeat, abandoned camp and fled. Shiduo's hungry troops, pressing their advantage, rushed into camp to seize military stores. Xingmi turned his troops and struck; Shiduo was utterly defeated, fled alone on horseback into the city, and then killed Gao Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Shiduo attacked with an army tens of thousands strong. Xingmi pretended defeat, abandoned his camp, and fled. Shiduo's hungry men, pressing their advantage, crowded into the camp to seize supplies; Xingmi wheeled about and struck them down. Shiduo was routed, rode alone into the city—and there killed Gao Pian.

sentences.zh: 行密聞駢死，縞軍向城哭三日，攻其西門，彥及師鐸奔於東塘，行密遂入揚州。

translations.literal: When Xingmi heard of Pian's death, he dressed his army in mourning white and wept toward the city for three days, then attacked the west gate. Yan and Shiduo fled to Dongtang, and Xingmi then entered Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Pian's death, Xingmi dressed his troops in white mourning and wept toward the walls for three days, then assaulted the west gate. Yan and Shiduo fled to Dongtang, and Xingmi entered Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 新五代史·世家是時，城中倉廩空虛，饑民相殺而食，其夫婦、父子自相牽，就屠賣之，屠者刲剔如羊豕。

translations.literal: At this time the granaries in the city were empty. Starving people killed one another for food; husbands and wives, fathers and sons dragged one another to butchers to be sold, and the butchers flayed and carved them like sheep and swine.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the city's granaries stood empty. The starving turned on one another for flesh; husbands and wives, fathers and sons led each other to the butcher's block to be sold, and the butchers skinned and carved them as they would sheep or swine.

sentences.zh: 行密不能守，欲走。

translations.literal: Xingmi could not hold the city and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi could not hold the city and prepared to flee.

sentences.zh: 而蔡州秦宗權遣其弟宗衡掠地淮南，彥及師鐸還自東塘，與宗衡合，行密閉城不敢出。

translations.literal: But Qin Zongquan of Caizhou sent his younger brother Zongheng to plunder Huainan. Yan and Shiduo returned from Dongtang and joined Zongheng; Xingmi shut the gates and dared not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Qin Zongquan of Caizhou sent his brother Zongheng to ravage Huainan. Yan and Shiduo came back from Dongtang and joined him, and Xingmi shut the gates and dared not venture out.

sentences.zh: 已而宗衡為偏將孫儒所殺，儒攻高郵破之，行密益懼。

translations.literal: Before long Zongheng was killed by the deputy general Sun Ru. Ru attacked Gaoyou and took it; Xingmi grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zongheng was killed by his own deputy Sun Ru, who then stormed and captured Gaoyou, and Xingmi's fear deepened.

sentences.zh: 其客袁襲曰：「吾以新集之眾守空城，而諸將多駢舊人，非有厚恩素信力制而心服之也。

translations.literal: His adviser Yuan Xi said: "We hold an empty city with a newly gathered host, and most of the generals are Pian's old followers—not men bound to us by deep favor, long-standing trust, or force of discipline that wins their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: His adviser Yuan Xi said, "We are holding an empty city with troops freshly gathered, and most of the generals are Gao Pian's old officers—men who owe us no deep kindness, no long trust, and no reason to submit in heart as well as in name."

sentences.zh: 今儒兵方盛，所攻必克，此諸將持兩端、因強弱、擇向背之時也。

translations.literal: "Now Ru's troops are at their height and whatever they attack they take—this is the moment when these generals will hedge, follow strength and weakness, and choose which side to face."
translations.idiomatic: "Sun Ru's army is at its peak and takes every place it strikes. This is the moment when those generals will sit on the fence, weigh the strong against the weak, and choose whom to follow."

sentences.zh: 海陵鎮使高霸，駢之舊將，必不為吾用。

translations.literal: "Gao Ba, military commissioner of Hailing, is one of Pian's old generals and will certainly not serve us."
translations.idiomatic: "Gao Ba of Hailing is one of Pian's veterans and will never serve us faithfully."

sentences.zh: 」行密乃以軍令召霸，霸率其兵入廣陵，行密欲使霸守天長，襲曰：「吾以疑霸而召之，其可復用乎？

translations.literal: " Xingmi then summoned Ba by military order. Ba led his troops into Guangling. Xingmi wished to have Ba defend Tianchang. Xi said: "We summoned Ba because we distrusted him—how can we employ him again?"
translations.idiomatic: " Xingmi summoned Ba by military order, and Ba marched his troops into Guangling. Xingmi meant to post him at Tianchang, but Xi said, "We called him in because we distrusted him—can we trust him again?"

sentences.zh: 且吾能勝儒，無所用霸，不幸不勝，天長豈吾有哉！

translations.literal: "Moreover, if we can defeat Ru we have no need of Ba; if by misfortune we cannot win, how could Tianchang remain ours!"
translations.idiomatic: "If we defeat Sun Ru, we have no need of him; if we fail, Tianchang will not be ours in any case!"

sentences.zh: 不如殺之，以並其眾。

translations.literal: "Better to kill him and absorb his troops."
translations.idiomatic: "Better to kill him and take his men for our own."

sentences.zh: 」行密因犒軍擒霸族之，得其兵數千。

translations.literal: " Xingmi, under pretext of rewarding the troops with a feast, seized Ba and exterminated his clan, gaining several thousand of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " At a feast held to reward the troops, Xingmi seized Ba, wiped out his clan, and took several thousand of his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 已而孫儒殺秦彥、畢師鐸，並其兵以攻行密。

translations.literal: Before long Sun Ru killed Qin Yan and Bi Shiduo, combined their armies, and attacked Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sun Ru killed Qin Yan and Bi Shiduo, united their forces with his own, and marched against Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密欲走海陵，襲曰：「海陵難守，而廬州吾舊治也，城廩完實，可為後圖。

translations.literal: Xingmi wished to flee to Hailing. Xi said: "Hailing is hard to defend, but Luzhou is territory I once ruled; its walls and granaries are intact and can serve as a base for later plans."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi meant to flee to Hailing, but Xi said, "Hailing cannot be held, whereas Luzhou is your old seat—its walls and stores are sound and can serve as a refuge for later designs."

sentences.zh: 」行密乃走廬州。

translations.literal: " Xingmi then fled to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingmi withdrew to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，未知所向，問襲曰：「吾欲卷甲倍道，西取洪州可乎？

translations.literal: After a long while, not knowing which way to turn, he asked Xi: "If I fold my armor and march at double speed to seize Hongzhou in the west, would that do?"
translations.idiomatic: After some time, still uncertain where to turn, he asked Xi, "Suppose I strike camp and march at forced pace to seize Hongzhou in the west—would that serve?"

sentences.zh: 」襲曰：「鐘傳新得江西，勢未可圖，而秦彥之入廣陵也，召池州刺史趙锽委以宣州。

translations.literal: " Xi said: "Zhong Chuan has newly taken Jiangxi and his power is not yet to be assailed. When Qin Yan entered Guangling he summoned Zhao Yin, Prefect of Chizhou, and entrusted Xuanzhou to him."
translations.idiomatic: " Xi replied, "Zhong Chuan has only lately taken Jiangxi and is not to be challenged yet. When Qin Yan entered Guangling he summoned Zhao Yin, prefect of Chizhou, and gave him Xuanzhou to hold."

sentences.zh: 今彥且死，锽失所恃，而守宣州非其本誌，且其為人非公敵，此可取也。

translations.literal: "Now Yan is about to die; Yin has lost his support. Holding Xuanzhou was never his original intent, and as a man he is no worthy public foe—this is a place we can take."
translations.idiomatic: "Yan is as good as dead, Yin has lost his patron, holding Xuanzhou was never his true aim, and he is no formidable enemy in his own right—there is our prize."

sentences.zh: 」行密乃引兵攻锽，戰於曷山，大敗之。

translations.literal: " Xingmi then led troops to attack Yin, fought at Mount He, and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingmi marched against Yin, met him at Mount He, and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 進圍宣州，锽棄城走，追及殺之，行密遂入宣州。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Xuanzhou, Yin abandoned the city and fled; pursued and killed, Xingmi then entered Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to besiege Xuanzhou; Yin abandoned the city and fled, was overtaken and killed, and Xingmi entered Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，復入揚州，唐拜行密淮南節度使。

translations.literal: That year he re-entered Yangzhou; Tang appointed Xingmi Military Governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: That year he re-entered Yangzhou, and the Tang court appointed him military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，加檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning he was further made Honorary Grand Mentor and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianning he was further made Honorary Grand Mentor and chancellor of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 行密以田頵守宣州，安仁義守潤州。

translations.literal: Xingmi posted Tian Run to defend Xuanzhou and An Renyi to defend Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi left Tian Run to hold Xuanzhou and An Renyi to hold Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 升州刺史馮弘鐸來附。

translations.literal: Feng Hongduo, Prefect of Shengzhou, came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hongduo, prefect of Shengzhou, came over to his side.

sentences.zh: 分遣頵等攻掠，自淮以南、江以東諸州皆下之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Run and others on raids of conquest; all prefectures south of the Huai and east of the Yangzi submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Run and others on campaigns of conquest until every prefecture south of the Huai and east of the Yangzi had fallen to him.

sentences.zh: 進攻蘇州，擒其刺史成及。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Suzhou, he captured its prefect Cheng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Suzhou and captured its prefect, Cheng Ji.

sentences.zh: 四年，兗州朱瑾奔於行密。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Zhu Jin of Yanzhou fled to Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhu Jin of Yanzhou fled to join him.

sentences.zh: 初，瑾為梁所攻，求救於晉，晉遣李承嗣將勁騎數千助瑾，瑾敗，因與俱奔行密。

translations.literal: Earlier Jin had been attacked by Liang and begged Jin for aid; Jin sent Li Chengsi leading several thousand crack horsemen to help him. Jin was defeated and fled together with Chengsi to Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu Jin had been hard pressed by Liang and appealed to the Jin court, which sent Li Chengsi at the head of several thousand elite horsemen to his aid. Defeated, Jin fled together with Chengsi to Xingmi's camp.

sentences.zh: 行密兵皆江、淮人，淮人輕弱，得瑾勁騎，而兵益振。

translations.literal: Xingmi's troops were all men of the Jianghuai; Huai men were deemed light and weak. Gaining Jin's crack cavalry, his army grew still more spirited.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi's soldiers were all natives of the Jianghuai region, regarded as slight and soft in the saddle; with Jin's hardened horsemen his army's morale rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 是歲，梁太祖遣葛從周、龐師古攻行密壽州，行密擊敗梁兵清口，殺師古，而從周收兵走，追至渒河，又大敗之。

translations.literal: That year the Liang Founder sent Ge Congzhou and Pang Shigu to attack Xingmi's Shouzhou. Xingmi defeated Liang troops at Qingkou, killed Shigu, and when Congzhou gathered his troops and fled, pursued to the Pi River and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Liang founder sent Ge Congzhou and Pang Shigu against Shouzhou. Xingmi shattered the Liang army at Qingkou and killed Shigu; Congzhou withdrew in disorder, was pursued to the Pi River, and defeated again.

sentences.zh: 五年，錢镠攻蘇州，及周本戰於白方湖，本敗，蘇州復入於越。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Qian Liu attacked Suzhou. Zhou Ben fought him at Baifang Lake; Ben was defeated and Suzhou returned to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Qian Liu attacked Suzhou. Zhou Ben met him at Baifang Lake, was defeated, and Suzhou passed back to Yue.

sentences.zh: 天復元年，遣李神福攻越，戰臨安，大敗之，擒其將顧全武以歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianfu he sent Li Shenfu to attack Yue, fought at Lin'an, routed them utterly, and captured their general Gu Quanwu, bringing him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianfu he sent Li Shenfu against Yue, routed the enemy at Lin'an, and brought back their general Gu Quanwu as a captive.

sentences.zh: 二年，馮弘鐸叛，襲宣州，及田頵戰於曷山，弘鐸敗，將入於海。

translations.literal: In the second year Feng Hongduo rebelled, raided Xuanzhou, and fought Tian Run at Mount He. Hongduo was defeated and was about to flee onto the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Feng Hongduo rebelled, struck at Xuanzhou, and was defeated by Tian Run at Mount He; he was preparing to take refuge on the open sea.

sentences.zh: 行密自至東塘邀之，使人謂弘鐸曰：「勝敗，用兵常事也，一戰之衄，何苦自棄於海島？

translations.literal: Xingmi went in person to Dongtang to intercept him and sent someone to say to Hongduo: "Victory and defeat are the common lot of war. Why, for one battle's setback, torment yourself with exile on some island?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi went in person to Dongtang to meet him and sent word: "Victory and defeat are the common lot of war. Why, for a single setback, condemn yourself to exile on some barren island?"

sentences.zh: 吾府雖小，猶足容君。

translations.literal: Though my headquarters is small, it can still shelter you."
translations.idiomatic: My domain is small, but it is still room enough for you."

sentences.zh: 」弘鐸感泣，行密從十餘騎，馳入其軍，以弘鐸為節度副使，以李神福代弘鐸為升州刺史。

translations.literal: " Hongduo wept with emotion. Xingmi, with a dozen horsemen, galloped into his army, made Hongduo Deputy Military Governor, and replaced him as Prefect of Shengzhou with Li Shenfu.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongduo wept with gratitude. Xingmi rode into his camp with barely a dozen followers, made him deputy military governor, and appointed Li Shenfu prefect of Shengzhou in his stead.

sentences.zh: 是歲，唐昭宗在岐，遣江淮宣諭使李儼拜行密東面諸道行營都統、檢校太師、中書令，封吳王。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Zhaozong of Tang was at Qi. He sent Li Yi, Commissioner to Announce and Console the Jianghuai, to appoint Xingmi Supreme Commander of the Eastern Circuit Campaign Armies, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoff him as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: That year, with Emperor Zhaozong at Qi, the court sent Li Yi from the Jianghuai mission to appoint Xingmi supreme commander of the eastern circuits, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 三年，以李神福為鄂嶽招討使以攻杜洪，荊南成汭救洪，神福敗之於君山。

translations.literal: In the third year he made Li Shenfu Commissioner for the Suppression of E-Yue to attack Du Hong. Cheng Ru of Jingnan came to Hong's rescue; Shenfu defeated him at Junshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he made Li Shenfu commissioner for the suppression of Ezhou and Yuezhou to attack Du Hong. Cheng Ru of Jingnan marched to Hong's relief and was defeated at Junshan.

sentences.zh: 梁兵攻青州，王師範來求救，遣王茂章救之，大敗梁兵，殺朱友寧。

translations.literal: Liang troops attacked Qingzhou; Wang Shifan came begging rescue. Xingmi sent Wang Maozhang to his aid; he routed Liang troops and killed Zhu Youning.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang forces besieged Qingzhou, Wang Shifan appealed for help. Xingmi sent Wang Maozhang, who routed the Liang army and killed Zhu Youning.

sentences.zh: 友寧，梁太祖子也，太祖大怒，自將以擊茂章，兵號二十萬，復為茂章所敗。

translations.literal: Youning was a son of the Liang Founder. The Founder was furious and led the attack on Maozhang in person with an army said to number two hundred thousand, but was defeated by Maozhang again.
translations.idiomatic: Youning was a son of the Liang founder, who flew into a rage and took the field in person with an army said to number two hundred thousand men—only to be beaten again by Maozhang.

sentences.zh: 田頵叛，襲升州，執李神福妻子歸於宣州。

translations.literal: Tian Run rebelled, raided Shengzhou, seized Li Shenfu's wife and children, and returned with them to Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Run rebelled, seized Shengzhou, took Li Shenfu's wife and children captive, and withdrew to Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密召神福以討頵，頵遣其將王壇逆之，又遣神福書，以其妻子招之。

translations.literal: Xingmi summoned Shenfu to campaign against Run. Run sent his general Wang Tan to oppose him and also sent Shenfu a letter, using his wife and children to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi summoned Shenfu to suppress Run. Run sent Wang Tan to block his path and wrote to Shenfu, offering the lives of his wife and children if he would defect.

sentences.zh: 神福曰：「吾以一卒從吳王起事，今為大將，忍背德而顧妻子乎？

translations.literal: Shenfu said: "I followed the Prince of Wu from a single soldier's rank when he first rose; now I am a great general—how could I bear to betray his grace for the sake of wife and children?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu said, "I followed the Prince of Wu when he had nothing but a single soldier's rank; now I command armies. Could I betray his trust for the sake of wife and children?"

sentences.zh: 」立斬其使以自絕，軍士聞之，皆感奮。

translations.literal: " He at once executed the envoy to cut off any retreat; when the soldiers heard of it, all were stirred and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: " He executed the envoy on the spot to make his choice irrevocable, and every soldier who heard of it was stirred to fight.

sentences.zh: 行至吉陽磯，頵執神福子承鼎以招之，神福叱左右射之，遂敗壇兵於吉陽。

translations.literal: When he reached Jiyang Ford, Run held Shenfu's son Chengdian to entice him. Shenfu shouted for his men to shoot; he then defeated Tan's troops at Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiyang Ford, Run produced Shenfu's son Chengdian to lure him over. Shenfu ordered his men to shoot the boy down and routed Wang Tan at Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 行密別遣臺濛擊頵，頵敗死。

translations.literal: Xingmi separately dispatched Tai Meng to strike Run; Run was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Tai Meng by another route; Run was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 初，頵及安仁義、朱延壽等皆從行密起微賤，及江、淮甫定，思漸休息，而三人者皆猛悍難制，頗欲除之，未有以發。

translations.literal: Earlier Run, An Renyi, Zhu Yanshou, and others had all risen with Xingmi from humble stations. Once the Jianghuai region was just settled, he wished gradually to rest, but all three were fierce and hard to control; he greatly wished to remove them but had no occasion to act.
translations.idiomatic: Run, An Renyi, Zhu Yanshou, and the rest had all risen with Xingmi from nothing. Once the Jianghuai region was pacified he longed for peace, but these three were ferocious and unruly, and though he wished to remove them he had found no pretext.

sentences.zh: 天復二年，錢镠為其將許再思等叛而圍之，再思召頵攻镠杭州，垂克，而行密納镠賂，命頵解兵，頵恨之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu Qian Liu was besieged when his generals Xu Zaisi and others rebelled. Zaisi summoned Run to attack Liu's Hangzhou. On the verge of success, Xingmi accepted bribes from Liu and ordered Run to withdraw his troops; Run bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu, Qian Liu was besieged when his generals Xu Zaisi and others rebelled. Zaisi called on Run to strike Hangzhou, and Run was on the brink of victory when Xingmi took Qian Liu's bribes and ordered him to stand down—an affront Run never forgave.

sentences.zh: 頵嘗計事廣陵，行密諸將多就頵求賂，而獄吏亦有所求。

translations.literal: Run once came to Guangling to discuss affairs; many of Xingmi's generals went to Run seeking bribes, and the prison clerks also made demands.
translations.idiomatic: On one visit to Guangling to discuss affairs, many of Xingmi's generals came to Run demanding bribes, and even the prison clerks held out their hands.

sentences.zh: 頵怒曰：「吏欲我下獄也！

translations.literal: Run said in anger: "Do these clerks want to throw me in prison!"
translations.idiomatic: Run flared up and said, "Do they mean to throw me in prison?!"

sentences.zh: 」歸而遂謀反。

translations.literal: " On returning he then plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " He went home and began plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 仁義聞之亦反，焚東塘以襲常州。

translations.literal: When Renyi heard of it he too rebelled, burned Dongtang, and raided Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi, hearing of it, rebelled as well, burned Dongtang, and struck at Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 常州刺史李遇出戰，望見仁義，大罵之。

translations.literal: Li Yu, Prefect of Changzhou, went out to fight; seeing Renyi in the distance, he cursed him loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, prefect of Changzhou, rode out to meet him and, catching sight of Renyi, hurled abuse at him.

sentences.zh: 仁義止其軍曰：「李遇乃敢辱我如此，其必有伏兵。

translations.literal: Renyi halted his army and said: "Li Yu dares insult me like this—there must be ambush troops."
translations.idiomatic: Renyi halted his army and said, "Li Yu dares insult me like that—he must have an ambush waiting."

sentences.zh: 」遂引軍卻，而伏兵果發，追至夾岡，仁義植幟解甲而食，遇兵不敢追，仁義復入潤州。

translations.literal: " He then withdrew his army, but ambush troops did spring forth. Pursued to Jiagang, Renyi planted banners, doffed armor, and ate; Yu's troops dared not pursue, and Renyi re-entered Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew back, and ambushers did spring up as he had feared. Pursued to Jiagang, he planted his banners, stripped his armor, and took a meal in plain sight; Yu's men dared not close in, and Renyi returned safely to Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密遣王茂章、李德誠、米誌誠等圍之。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent Wang Maozhang, Li Decheng, Mi Zhicheng, and others to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Wang Maozhang, Li Decheng, Mi Zhicheng, and others to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 吳之軍中推朱瑾善槊，誌誠善射，皆為第一。

translations.literal: In Wu's army Zhu Jin was acclaimed first with the spear and Mi Zhicheng first with the bow.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wu army Zhu Jin was reckoned supreme with the spear and Mi Zhicheng supreme with the bow.

sentences.zh: 而仁義嘗以射自負，曰：「誌城之弓十，不當瑾槊之一；

translations.literal: Renyi once prided himself on archery and said: "Ten of Zhicheng's bows are not worth one of Jin's spears;
translations.idiomatic: Renyi prided himself on his bow and once boasted, "Ten of Zhicheng's bows are not worth one of Jin's spears;

sentences.zh: 瑾槊之十，不當仁義弓之一。

translations.literal: ten of Jin's spears are not worth one of Renyi's bows."
translations.idiomatic: and ten of Jin's spears are not worth one of Renyi's bow."

sentences.zh: 」每與茂章等戰，必命中而後發，以此吳軍畏之，不敢進。

translations.literal: " In every battle with Maozhang and the others he would not shoot until he was certain of a hit; for this the Wu army feared him and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: " In every clash with Maozhang and the rest he would not loose an arrow until he was sure of his mark, and the Wu troops feared him so much they would not press forward.

sentences.zh: 行密亦欲招降之，仁義猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Xingmi also wished to win him by surrender, but Renyi hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi wished to accept his surrender, but Renyi wavered and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 茂章乘其怠，穴地道而入，執仁義，斬於廣陵。

translations.literal: Maozhang seized his moment of slackness, tunneled in through an underground passage, seized Renyi, and executed him at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang caught him off guard, tunneled into the fortress, seized him, and had him beheaded at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 延壽者，行密夫人朱氏之弟也。

translations.literal: Yanshou was the younger brother of Xingmi's consort, the Zhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou was the younger brother of Lady Zhu, Xingmi's consort.

sentences.zh: 頵及仁義之將叛也，行密疑之，乃陽為目疾，每接延壽使者，必錯亂其所見以示之。

translations.literal: When Run and Renyi were about to rebel, Xingmi grew suspicious of him and feigned eye disease; whenever he received Yanshou's envoys he would deliberately confuse what he saw to show them.
translations.idiomatic: As Run and Renyi prepared to rebel, Xingmi grew suspicious of Yanshou and pretended to suffer from failing sight; whenever Yanshou's envoys came he would deliberately mistake what lay before him.

sentences.zh: 嘗行，故觸柱而仆，朱夫人扶之，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: Once while walking he deliberately struck a pillar and fell. Lady Zhu supported him; only after a long while did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: Once, walking abroad, he deliberately struck a pillar and collapsed. Lady Zhu helped him up, and he lay as though unconscious for a long while before coming to.

sentences.zh: 泣曰：「吾業成而喪其目，是天廢我也！

translations.literal: Weeping he said: "My enterprise is accomplished yet I have lost my eyes—Heaven has cast me aside!"
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he said, "My work is done and I have lost my sight—Heaven has cast me aside!"

sentences.zh: 吾兒子皆不足以任事，得延壽付之，吾無恨矣。

translations.literal: "My sons are none of them fit to bear affairs. If I can entrust power to Yanshou, I shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: "My sons are not fit to bear this burden. If I can entrust affairs to Yanshou, I shall die content."

sentences.zh: 」夫人喜，急召延壽。

translations.literal: " His consort was delighted and urgently summoned Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: " His wife was overjoyed and sent for Yanshou at once.

sentences.zh: 延壽至，行密迎之寢門，刺殺之，出朱夫人以嫁之。

translations.literal: When Yanshou arrived, Xingmi met him at the bedchamber door, stabbed and killed him, then sent Lady Zhu out to be married off.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshou arrived, Xingmi met him at the bedchamber door and ran him through, then sent Lady Zhu away to marry another man.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年，遣劉存攻鄂州，焚其城，城中兵突圍而出，諸將請急擊之，存曰：「擊之復入，則城愈固，聽其去，城可取也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianyou he sent Liu Cun to attack Ezhou and burn its walls. Troops in the city broke out of encirclement. The generals begged to strike them at once. Cun said: "If we strike and they re-enter, the city will be all the harder to take. Let them go—the city can then be seized."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianyou he sent Liu Cun against Ezhou and burned its walls. The garrison broke out of the encirclement, and the generals urged an immediate pursuit. Cun said, "If we strike and they slip back inside, the city will only grow harder to take. Let them go—the city will be ours."

sentences.zh: 」是日城破，執杜洪，斬於廣陵。

translations.literal: " That same day the city fell. Du Hong was seized and executed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day the city fell; Du Hong was taken and beheaded at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 九月，梁兵攻破襄州，趙匡凝奔於行密。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Liang troops broke Xiangzhou; Zhao Kuangning fled to Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liang forces captured Xiangzhou, and Zhao Kuangning fled to Xingmi's protection.

sentences.zh: 十一月，行密卒，年五十四，謚曰武忠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xingmi died at the age of fifty-four. His posthumous title was Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Xingmi died at the age of fifty-four; his posthumous title was Wuzhong, Martial and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子渥立。

translations.literal: His son Wo succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 溥僭號，追尊行密為太祖武皇帝，陵曰興陵。

translations.literal: When Pu usurped the imperial title, he posthumously honored Xingmi as Emperor Wu, the founding ancestor, with the mausoleum named Xingling.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu declared himself emperor, he posthumously honored Xingmi as Emperor Wu, founding ancestor of the line, with the mausoleum Xingling.

sentences.zh: 渥字承天，行密長子也。

translations.literal: Wo, courtesy name Chengtian, was Xingmi's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Wo, whose courtesy name was Chengtian, was Yang Xingmi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 行密病，出渥為宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: When Xingmi fell ill, he sent Wo out as Military Commissioner of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi fell ill, he posted Wo to Xuanzhou as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 右衙指揮使徐溫私謂渥曰：「今王有疾而出嫡嗣，必有奸臣之謀，若它日召子，非溫使者慎無應命。

translations.literal: Right Guards Commander Xu Wen said privately to Wo: "Now the Prince is ill and has sent out his legitimate heir—there must be a traitor's plot. If someday you are summoned, unless the envoy is from Wen, be careful not to obey."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen, commander of the right guards, took Wo aside and said, "The Prince is ill and has sent his heir away from court—someone is surely plotting treason. If you are summoned later, do not answer unless the messenger is mine."

sentences.zh: 」渥涕泣謝溫而去。

translations.literal: " Wo wept, thanked Wen, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Wo wept, thanked him, and left.

sentences.zh: 行密病甚，命判官周隱作符召渥，隱慮渥幼弱不任事，勸行密用舊將有威望者代主軍政，乃薦大將劉威，行密未許。

translations.literal: Xingmi's illness grew grave; he ordered his aide Zhou Yin to draft a tally summoning Wo. Yin feared Wo was young and weak and unfit for affairs, and urged Xingmi to put an old general of prestige in charge of military and civil government instead; he recommended the great general Liu Wei, but Xingmi did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: As Xingmi's illness worsened, he ordered his aide Zhou Yin to draft a summons for Wo. Yin judged the heir too young and weak to rule and urged Xingmi to entrust military and civil affairs to a seasoned general of standing instead, recommending Liu Wei—but Xingmi refused.

sentences.zh: 溫與嚴可求入問疾，行密以隱議告之，溫等大驚，遽詣隱所計事。

translations.literal: Wen and Yan Keqiu came in to inquire after his health; Xingmi told them of Yin's plan. Wen and the others were greatly alarmed and hurried to Yin's quarters to discuss the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Yan Keqiu came to inquire after his health, and Xingmi told them what Yin had proposed. They were horrified and rushed at once to Yin's office.

sentences.zh: 隱未出，而溫見隱作召符猶在案上，急取遣之。

translations.literal: Before Yin emerged, Wen saw the summons Yin had drafted still on the desk and seized it to dispatch at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had not yet come out when Wen spotted the draft summons still on the desk, snatched it up, and sent it off at once.

sentences.zh: 渥見溫使，乃行。

translations.literal: When Wo saw Wen's envoy, he set out.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo saw Wen's messenger, he set out for Guangling.

sentences.zh: 行密卒，渥嗣立，召周隱罵曰：「汝欲賣吾國者，復何面目見楊氏乎？

translations.literal: Xingmi died; Wo succeeded him. He summoned Zhou Yin and cursed him: "You who wished to sell out my state—what face have you left to show the Yang clan?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi died and Wo succeeded him. He summoned Zhou Yin and raged, "You meant to sell out my realm—how dare you show your face to the house of Yang?"

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: " He then had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: " He had him executed.

sentences.zh: 以王茂章為宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: He made Wang Maozhang Military Commissioner of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wang Maozhang military commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 渥之入也，多輦宣州庫物以歸廣陵，茂章惜而不與，渥怒，命李簡以兵五千圍之，茂章奔於錢塘。

translations.literal: When Wo had entered Guangling he had carted much of Xuanzhou's treasury goods back; Maozhang begrudged yielding them and refused. Wo was angry and ordered Li Jian with five thousand troops to besiege him; Maozhang fled to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: On entering Guangling, Wo had hauled away much of Xuanzhou's treasury stores; Maozhang refused to surrender the rest, and Wo in fury sent Li Jian with five thousand men to besiege him. Maozhang fled to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年二月，劉存取岳州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Tianyou, Liu Cun took Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year of Tianyou, Liu Cun captured Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，江西鐘傳卒，其子匡時代立，傳養子延規怨不得立，以兵攻匡時。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Zhong Chuan of Jiangxi died; his son Kuangshi succeeded him. Chuan's adopted son Yan Gui, resentful that he was not enthroned, attacked Kuangshi with troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhong Chuan of Jiangxi died and his son Kuangshi succeeded him. Chuan's adopted son Yan Gui, bitter at being passed over, raised troops against Kuangshi.

sentences.zh: 渥遣秦裴率兵攻之。

translations.literal: Wo sent Qin Pei leading troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wo sent Qin Pei at the head of an army to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 九月，克洪州，執匡時及司馬陳象以歸，斬象於市，赦匡時。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he took Hongzhou, seized Kuangshi and Vice Prefect Chen Xiang and brought them back, executed Xiang in the marketplace, and pardoned Kuangshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he took Hongzhou, seized Kuangshi and Vice Prefect Chen Xiang, executed Xiang in the marketplace, and pardoned Kuangshi.

sentences.zh: 以秦裴為江西制置使。

translations.literal: He made Qin Pei Commissioner for the Pacification of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He made Qin Pei commissioner for the pacification of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖代唐，改元開平，渥仍稱天祐。

translations.literal: The Liang Founder replaced Tang and changed the era name to Kaiping; Wo still used Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang founder supplanted Tang and proclaimed the era Kaiping, Wo still dated his reign by Tianyou.

sentences.zh: 鄂州劉存、岳州陳知新以舟師伐楚，敗於瀏陽，楚人執存及知新以歸。

translations.literal: Liu Cun of Ezhou and Chen Zhixin of Yuezhou led a fleet to attack Chu and were defeated at Liuyang; the Chu seized Cun and Zhixin and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cun of Ezhou and Chen Zhixin of Yuezhou led a fleet against Chu, were defeated at Liuyang, and were taken captive to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 楚王馬殷素聞其名，皆欲活之，存等大罵殷曰：「昔歲宣城脫吾刃下，今日之敗，乃天亡我，我肯事汝以求活耶？

translations.literal: Chu King Ma Yin had long heard their names and wished to spare them both. Cun and the others cursed Yin loudly: "Last year at Xuancheng you slipped from beneath our blades; today's defeat is Heaven destroying us. Would I serve you to save my life?"
translations.idiomatic: King Ma Yin of Chu had long admired them and wished to spare their lives. Cun and the others cursed him: "Last year at Xuancheng you slipped from under our blades; today's defeat is Heaven's judgment on us. Do you think I would serve you to live?"

sentences.zh: 我豈負楊氏者！

translations.literal: Would I betray the Yang clan!
translations.idiomatic: I am no traitor to the Yang house!

sentences.zh: 」殷知不可屈，乃殺之，岳州復入於楚。

translations.literal: " Yin knew they could not be bent and had them killed; Yuezhou returned to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin saw they would not yield and had them executed; Yuezhou passed back to Chu.

sentences.zh: 初，渥之入廣陵也，留帳下兵三千於宣州，以其腹心陳璠、範遇將之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wo entered Guangling, he left three thousand personal troops at Xuanzhou under his trusted men Chen Fan and Fan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo first entered Guangling he had left three thousand of his personal troops at Xuanzhou under his confidants Chen Fan and Fan Yu.

sentences.zh: 既入立，惡徐溫典牙兵，召璠等為東院馬軍以自衛。

translations.literal: Once enthroned he disliked Xu Wen's command of the guard troops and summoned Fan and the others as Eastern Court Horse Army to guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he resented Xu Wen's control of the guard regiments and recalled Fan and the others as the Eastern Court Horse Army to protect himself.

sentences.zh: 而溫與左衙都指揮使張顥皆行密時舊將，又有立渥之功，共惡璠等侵其權。

translations.literal: But Wen and Left Guards Commander-in-Chief Zhang Hao were both old generals from Xingmi's day and had merit in enthroning Wo; together they hated Fan and the others for encroaching on their power.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Zhang Hao, commander of the left guards, were both veterans of Xingmi's rise and had helped place Wo on the throne; together they resented Fan and his faction for usurping their authority.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，渥視事，璠等侍側，溫、顥擁牙兵入，拽璠等下，斬之，渥不能止，由是失政，而心憤未能發，溫等益不自安。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Wo assumed office with Fan and the others attending at his side. Wen and Hao led the guard troops in, dragged Fan and the others down, and beheaded them. Wo could not stop it; from this he lost control of government, yet his rage could not find outlet, and Wen and the others grew still more uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Wo took up rule with Fan and his men at his side. Wen and Hao marched the guard regiments in, dragged Fan and the others down, and beheaded them before Wo could intervene. From that day he was ruler in name only, burning with resentment he dared not show, while Wen and his party grew ever more fearful.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，溫、顥共遣盜入寢中殺渥，渥說群盜能反殺溫等者皆為刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year Wen and Hao jointly sent assassins into the bedchamber to kill Wo. Wo told the band: whoever could turn and kill Wen and the others would be made a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year Wen and Hao sent assassins into the royal chambers. Wo promised the killers that whoever turned on Wen and his party would be made a prefect.

sentences.zh: 群盜皆諾，惟紀祥不從，執渥縊殺之，時年二十三，謚曰景。

translations.literal: The band all agreed, but Ji Xiang alone refused; they seized Wo and strangled him. He was twenty-three; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: They all agreed except Ji Xiang, who seized Wo and strangled him instead. He was twenty-three; his posthumous title was Jing.

sentences.zh: 弟隆演立。

translations.literal: His younger brother Longyan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Longyan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 溥僭號，追尊渥為烈宗景皇帝，陵曰紹陵。

translations.literal: When Pu usurped the imperial title, he posthumously honored Wo as Emperor Jing, Liezong, with the mausoleum named Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu declared himself emperor, he posthumously honored Wo as Emperor Jing of the Liezong line, with the mausoleum Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 隆演字鴻源，行密第二子也。

translations.literal: Longyan, courtesy name Hongyuan, was Xingmi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Longyan, whose courtesy name was Hongyuan, was Yang Xingmi's second son.

sentences.zh: 初名瀛，又名渭。

translations.literal: His original name was Ying; he was also called Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been named Ying and was also known as Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，溫、顥之弒渥也，約分其地以臣於梁，及渥死，顥欲背約自立。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wen and Hao murdered Wo, they had agreed to divide the territory and submit as vassals to Liang. After Wo's death Hao wished to break the pact and rule on his own.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen and Hao had murdered Wo they had agreed to partition the realm and submit to Liang as vassals. Once Wo was dead, Hao meant to break the pact and seize power for himself.

sentences.zh: 溫患之，問其客嚴可求，可求曰：「顥雖剛愎，而暗於成事，此易為也。

translations.literal: Wen was troubled by this and asked his adviser Yan Keqiu. Keqiu said: "Though Hao is stubborn and self-willed, he is dim at bringing things to completion—this is easy to manage."
translations.idiomatic: Wen was alarmed and consulted Yan Keqiu, who said, "Hao is obstinate but dull at finishing what he starts—this can be turned aside easily."

sentences.zh: 」明日，顥列劍戟府中，召諸將議事，自大將朱瑾而下，皆去衛從然後入。

translations.literal: " The next day Hao arrayed swords and halberds in the headquarters and summoned the generals to council; from the great general Zhu Jin downward, all had to dismiss their escorts before entering.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Hao lined the headquarters with swords and halberds and summoned the generals to council; from Zhu Jin downward, every man had to leave his escort outside before entering.

sentences.zh: 顥問諸將，誰當立者，諸將莫敢對。

translations.literal: Hao asked the generals who ought to be enthroned; none dared answer.
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked who should be enthroned; no one dared reply.

sentences.zh: 顥三問，可求前密啟曰：「方今四境多虞，非公主之不可，然恐為之太速。

translations.literal: Hao asked three times. Keqiu stepped forward and whispered: "The four borders are full of alarms; none but a prince of the house will do—yet I fear acting too swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: Hao pressed the question three times. Keqiu stepped forward and whispered, "The realm is beset on every side—only a prince of the house will do, yet I fear we move too fast."

sentences.zh: 且今外有劉威、陶雅、李簡、李遇，皆先王一等人也，公雖自立，未知此輩能降心以事公否。

translations.literal: "Moreover, outside there are Liu Wei, Tao Ya, Li Jian, and Li Yu—all men of the late king's first rank. Though you might rule on your own, it is unknown whether they would bend their hearts to serve you."
translations.idiomatic: "Outside stand Liu Wei, Tao Ya, Li Jian, and Li Yu—men of the late king's first rank. Even if you seize the throne yourself, who knows whether they will bow to you?"

sentences.zh: 不若輔立幼主，漸以歲時，待其歸心，然後可也。

translations.literal: "Better to support and enthrone the young lord, and little by little, as the years pass, wait until hearts return to you—then it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: "Better to set up the young heir and win their loyalty over time—then you may act."

sentences.zh: 」顥不能對。

translations.literal: " Hao could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao had no answer.

sentences.zh: 可求因趨出，書一教內袖中，率諸將入賀，諸將莫知所為。

translations.literal: Keqiu then hurried out, wrote an instruction and hid it in his sleeve, and led the generals in to offer congratulations; the generals did not know what was afoot.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu slipped out, drafted an instruction and hid it in his sleeve, then led the generals in to offer congratulations—they had no idea what he intended.

sentences.zh: 及出教宣之，乃渥母史氏教，言楊氏創業艱難，而嗣王不幸，隆演以次當立，告諸將以無負楊氏而善事之。

translations.literal: When the instruction was produced and proclaimed, it was an order from Wo's mother, Lady Shi, stating that the Yang clan's founding had been arduous, the heir unfortunate, and Longyan next in line to rule; it told the generals not to fail the Yang and to serve him well.
translations.idiomatic: When he produced and read the instruction, it proved to be an order from Wo's mother Lady Shi: the Yang house had built its realm through hardship, the heir had met an untimely end, and Longyan was next in line; the generals must not betray the Yang and must serve him faithfully.

sentences.zh: 辭旨激切，聞者感動。

translations.literal: The words were impassioned; all who heard were moved.
translations.idiomatic: The words were fierce and moving; every man who heard them was stirred.

sentences.zh: 顥氣色皆沮，卒無能為，隆演乃得立。

translations.literal: Hao's color fell utterly; in the end he could do nothing, and Longyan was able to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's face fell; in the end he could do nothing, and Longyan took the throne.

sentences.zh: 顥由此與溫有隙，諷隆演出溫潤州。

translations.literal: From this Hao and Wen had a rift; Hao urged Longyan to send Wen out to Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Hao and Wen were at odds, and Hao persuaded Longyan to post Wen to Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 可求謂溫曰：「今舍衙兵而出外郡，禍行至矣。

translations.literal: Keqiu said to Wen: "Now you abandon the guard troops and go to an outer prefecture—disaster is at hand."
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu warned Wen, "If you leave the guard regiments for some outer prefecture, you are walking into your own death."

sentences.zh: 」溫患之，可求因說顥曰：「公與徐溫同受顧托，議者謂公奪其衙兵，是將殺之於外，信乎？

translations.literal: " Wen was troubled. Keqiu then said to Hao: "You and Xu Wen received the late king's charge together. Gossip says you stripped him of the guard troops intending to kill him abroad—is that true?"
translations.idiomatic: " Wen was alarmed. Keqiu then told Hao, "You and Xu Wen were entrusted together. Men say you stripped him of the guards to murder him in the provinces—is that your plan?"

sentences.zh: 」顥曰：「事已行矣，安可止乎？

translations.literal: " Hao said: "The matter is already in motion—how can it be stopped?"
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "The order has already gone out—how can I recall it?"

sentences.zh: 」可求曰：「甚易也。

translations.literal: " Keqiu said: "Very easy."
translations.idiomatic: " Keqiu said, "That is easily undone."

sentences.zh: 」明日，從乂頁與諸將造溫，可求陽責溫曰：「古人不忘一飯之恩，況公楊氏三世之將，今幼嗣新立，多事之時，乃求居外以茍安乎？

translations.literal: " The next day, following Keqiu's lead, the generals went to Wen. Keqiu openly rebuked Wen: "Men of old did not forget the grace of a single meal—how much more you, a general of the Yang clan for three generations! Now the young heir is newly enthroned in troubled times, and you seek to live abroad for your own ease?"
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Keqiu led the generals to Wen's quarters and rebuked him before them all: "Men of old did not forget a single meal's kindness—and you, a general of three Yang rulers, would abandon a boy king in troubled times to seek safety in the provinces?"

sentences.zh: 」溫亦陽謝曰：「公等見留，不願去也。

translations.literal: " Wen also feigned thanks and said: "You gentlemen have detained me—I do not wish to leave."
translations.idiomatic: " Wen played along and thanked them: "You have kept me here—I have no wish to go."

sentences.zh: 」由是不行。

translations.literal: " Thus the posting did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: " The transfer was called off.

sentences.zh: 行軍副使李承嗣與張顥善，覺可求有附溫意，諷顥使客夜刺殺之，客刺可求不能中。

translations.literal: Campaign Deputy Li Chengsi was friendly with Zhang Hao; perceiving that Keqiu favored Wen, he urged Hao to send a guest to assassinate him by night. The assassin struck Keqiu but missed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengsi, campaign deputy, was close to Zhang Hao and, seeing Keqiu's leanings toward Wen, urged Hao to send an assassin by night. The man struck but missed.

sentences.zh: 明日，可求詣溫，謀先殺顥，陰遣鐘章選壯士三十人，就衙堂斬顥，因以弒渥之罪歸之。

translations.literal: The next day Keqiu went to Wen and plotted to kill Hao first; secretly he sent Zhong Zhang to select thirty stalwarts who cut Hao down in the headquarters hall and laid on him the crime of murdering Wo.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Keqiu went to Wen and plotted Hao's death; secretly he sent Zhong Zhang with thirty picked men to cut Hao down in the headquarters and charged him with murdering Wo.

sentences.zh: 溫由是專政，隆演備位而已。

translations.literal: From this Wen monopolized government; Longyan held the throne in name only.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Wen held real power and Longyan reigned in name alone.

sentences.zh: 六月，撫州危全諷叛，攻洪州，袁州彭彥章、吉州彭釬、信州危仔倡皆起兵叛。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Wei Quanfeng of Fuzhou rebelled and attacked Hongzhou; Peng Yanzhang of Yuanzhou, Peng Gan of Jizhou, and Wei Zaichang of Xinzhou all raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Wei Quanfeng of Fuzhou rebelled and attacked Hongzhou, while Peng Yanzhang of Yuanzhou, Peng Gan of Jizhou, and Wei Zaichang of Xinzhou all rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 隆演召嚴可求問誰可用者。

translations.literal: Longyan summoned Yan Keqiu and asked who could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Longyan summoned Yan Keqiu and asked whom he could send.

sentences.zh: 可求薦周本，時本方攻蘇州敗歸，慚不肯出，可求強起之。

translations.literal: Keqiu recommended Zhou Ben, who had just returned defeated from attacking Suzhou on Wu's behalf and, ashamed, refused to go out; Keqiu forced him to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu recommended Zhou Ben, who had lately returned defeated from the Suzhou campaign and in shame refused the command until Keqiu pressed him to accept.

sentences.zh: 本曰：「蘇州之敗，非怯也，乃上將權輕，而下多專命爾。

translations.literal: Ben said: "The defeat at Suzhou was not from cowardice but because the commanding general's authority was light and subordinates too often acted on their own orders."
translations.idiomatic: Ben said, "We lost Suzhou not from cowardice but because the commander lacked authority and his subordinates took their own orders."

sentences.zh: 若必見任，願無用偏裨。

translations.literal: "If I am truly to be entrusted, I wish not to use deputy commanders."
translations.idiomatic: "If you truly mean to entrust me with this, give me no deputy commanders."

sentences.zh: 」乃請兵七千。

translations.literal: " He then requested seven thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked for seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 戰於象牙潭，敗之，執全諷、彥章，而玕奔於楚，仔倡奔於錢塘。

translations.literal: He fought at Ivory Pool Ford, defeated them, seized Quanfeng and Yanzhang; Gan fled to Chu and Zaichang fled to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: He met them at Ivory Pool Ford, routed their army, and seized Quanfeng and Yanzhang; Gan fled to Chu and Zaichang to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 全諷至廣陵，諸將議曰：「昔先王攻趙锽，全諷屢餉給吳軍。

translations.literal: When Quanfeng reached Guangling the generals deliberated: "In the past when the late king attacked Zhao Yin, Quanfeng repeatedly supplied the Wu army."
translations.idiomatic: When Quanfeng was brought to Guangling the generals said, "When the late king attacked Zhao Yin, Quanfeng repeatedly supplied our armies."

sentences.zh: 」乃釋不殺。

translations.literal: " They then released him without killing.
translations.idiomatic: " They spared his life.

sentences.zh: 初，全諷欲舉兵也，錢镠送王茂章於梁，道過全諷，謂曰：「聞公欲大舉，願見公兵，以知濟否。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Quanfeng wished to raise troops, Qian Liu was escorting Wang Maozhang to Liang; passing Quanfeng's territory he said: "I hear you mean a great campaign—I wish to see your troops to know whether you can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Quanfeng prepared to rebel, Qian Liu was escorting Wang Maozhang toward Liang territory and, passing through, said, "I hear you mean to rise in arms—let me see your troops and judge whether you can succeed."

sentences.zh: 」全諷陣兵，與茂章登城望之，茂章曰：「我素事吳，吳兵三等，如公此眾，可當其下將爾，非得益兵十萬不可。

translations.literal: " Quanfeng arrayed his troops; he and Maozhang climbed the wall to look. Maozhang said: "I long served Wu. Wu troops come in three grades—a host like yours would match only their lowest officers; you would need another hundred thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: " Quanfeng drew up his men and climbed the wall with Maozhang to survey them. Maozhang said, "I served Wu for years. Their troops come in three grades—a force like yours would match only their lowest officers; you would need another hundred thousand men."

sentences.zh: 」而全諷卒以此敗。

translations.literal: " In the end Quanfeng was defeated for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end that was exactly why he failed.

sentences.zh: 八年，徐溫領升州刺史，治舟師於金陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Xu Wen took charge as Prefect of Shengzhou and built a fleet at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Xu Wen became prefect of Shengzhou and built a fleet at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 宣州李遇自行密時為大將，勛位已高，憤溫用事，嘗曰：「徐溫何人？

translations.literal: Li Yu of Xuanzhou had been a great general since Xingmi's day; his merit and rank were already high. He resented Wen's hold on power and once said: "Who is Xu Wen?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu of Xuanzhou had been a great general since Xingmi's day and resented Wen's dominance. He once said, "Who is Xu Wen?"

sentences.zh: 吾猶未識，而驟至於此。

translations.literal: "I do not even know him, yet he has suddenly risen to this."
translations.idiomatic: "I hardly knew him, and now he stands above me."

sentences.zh: 」溫聞之，怒，遣柴再用以兵送王壇代遇，且召之。

translations.literal: " When Wen heard of it he was angry and sent Chai Zaiyong with troops to escort Wang Tan to replace Yu and also summoned Yu.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen heard of it, flew into a rage, and sent Chai Zaiyong with troops to install Wang Tan in Yu's place while summoning Yu to court.

sentences.zh: 遇疑不受命，再用圍之，隆演使客將何蕘諭遇使自歸。

translations.literal: Yu suspected he would not be allowed to obey and refused; Zaiyong besieged him. Longyan sent his guest-general He Rao to persuade Yu to surrender of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Yu suspected a trap and refused to obey; Zaiyong besieged him. Longyan sent He Rao to persuade him to submit peacefully.

sentences.zh: 蕘因說曰：「公若欲反，可殺蕘以示眾，若本無心，何不隨蕘以出？

translations.literal: Rao then said: "If you wish to rebel, you may kill Rao to show the crowd; if you have no such intent, why not follow Rao out?"
translations.idiomatic: Rao said, "If you mean to rebel, kill me before your men to prove it; if your heart is loyal, why not come out with me?"

sentences.zh: 」遇自以無反心，乃隨蕘出，溫諷再用伺其出，殺之，並族其家。

translations.literal: " Yu, believing he had no rebellious heart, followed Rao out. Wen hinted to Zaiyong to watch for his emergence and kill him, and exterminated his clan as well.
translations.idiomatic: " Believing himself innocent, Yu followed Rao out. Wen signaled Zaiyong to strike as he emerged, killed him, and wiped out his clan.

sentences.zh: 九年，溫率將吏進隆演位太師、中書令、吳王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Wen led officers and clerks to advance Longyan to Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Wen led the court in advancing Longyan to Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 溫為行軍司馬、鎮海軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Wen became Acting Commander of the Campaign Army, Military Governor of Zhenhai Army, and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Wen became acting campaign commander, military governor of the Zhenhai army, and chancellor of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 陳章攻楚取岳州，執其刺史苑玫。

translations.literal: Chen Zhang attacked Chu, took Yuezhou, and seized its prefect Yuan Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhang attacked Chu, captured Yuezhou, and took its prefect Yuan Mei prisoner.

sentences.zh: 十年，越人攻常州，徐溫敗之於無錫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Yue people attacked Changzhou; Xu Wen defeated them at Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Yue attacked Changzhou and Xu Wen defeated them at Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 梁遣王茂章攻壽春，溫敗之霍丘。

translations.literal: Liang sent Wang Maozhang to attack Shouchun; Wen defeated him at Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Wang Maozhang against Shouchun; Wen routed him at Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，封徐溫齊國公、兩浙都招討使，始鎮潤州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Xu Wen was enfeoffed Duke of Qi and Supreme Commissioner for the Suppression of the Two Zhe circuits, and first established his seat at Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Xu Wen was made Duke of Qi and supreme commissioner for the Two Zhe circuits, and established his base at Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 留其子知訓為行軍副使，秉政，而大事溫遙決之。

translations.literal: He left his son Zhixun as Campaign Deputy to hold government, while great affairs Wen decided from afar.
translations.idiomatic: He left his son Zhixun as campaign deputy to run daily affairs while he decided great matters from afar.

sentences.zh: 冬，浚楊林江，水中出火，可以燃。

translations.literal: In winter they dredged the Yanglin River; fire emerged from the water and could be kindled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they dredged the Yanglin River, and fire burst from the water that men could kindle and burn.

sentences.zh: 十三年，宿衛將李球、馬謙挾隆演登樓，取庫兵以誅知訓，陣於門橋。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the palace guards Li Qiu and Ma Qian seized Longyan up the tower, took arsenal weapons to execute Zhixun, and formed battle lines at the gate bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the palace guards Li Qiu and Ma Qian seized Longyan, armed themselves from the arsenal to kill Zhixun, and drew up before the gate bridge.

sentences.zh: 知訓與戰，頻卻，朱瑾適自外來，以一騎前視其陣，曰：「此不足為也。

translations.literal: Zhixun fought them but was repeatedly driven back. Zhu Jin happened to come from outside, rode forward alone to view their formation, and said: "This is nothing to worry over."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun fought but was driven back again and again. Zhu Jin rode in from outside, surveyed the rebel line alone, and said, "This is nothing."

sentences.zh: 」因反顧一麾，外兵爭進，遂斬球、謙，而亂兵皆潰。

translations.literal: " He then turned and waved once; the outside troops rushed forward in contention, beheaded Qiu and Qian, and the mutinous soldiers all fled.
translations.idiomatic: " He wheeled about and waved once; the outside troops surged forward, cut down Qiu and Qian, and the mutineers scattered.

sentences.zh: 十四年，徐溫徙治金陵。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Xu Wen moved his administration to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Xu Wen moved his seat to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遣王祺會洪、袁、信三州兵攻虔、韶，久之不克。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he sent Wang Qi to join troops from Hong, Yuan, and Xin prefectures to attack Qian and Shao; after a long while they could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he sent Wang Qi with troops from Hong, Yuan, and Xin to attack Qian and Shao, but after a long siege they could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 祺病，以劉信代之。

translations.literal: Qi fell ill and Liu Xin replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi fell ill and Liu Xin took his place.

sentences.zh: 四月，副都統朱瑾殺徐知訓，瑾自殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zhu Jin killed Xu Zhixun, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhu Jin, deputy commander-in-chief, killed Xu Zhixun and then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 潤州徐知誥聞亂，率兵入，殺唐宣諭使李儼以止亂，遂秉政。

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao of Runzhou, hearing of the turmoil, led troops in, killed Tang's Commissioner to Announce and Console Li Yi to stop the disorder, and then held government.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao at Runzhou, hearing of the chaos, marched in, killed the Tang commissioner Li Yi to quell the disturbance, and seized control of government.

sentences.zh: 徐氏之專政也，隆演幼懦，不能自持，而知訓尤淩侮之。

translations.literal: During the Xu clan's monopoly of government, Longyan was young and timid and could not hold his own, while Zhixun especially bullied and insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xu domination Longyan was young, timid, and powerless, and Zhixun above all delighted in humiliating him.

sentences.zh: 嘗飲酒樓上，命優人高貴卿侍酒，知訓為參軍，隆演鶉衣髽髻為蒼鶻。

translations.literal: Once drinking in a tower he ordered the actor Gao Guiqing to serve wine; Zhixun played the military aide and Longyan, in quail coat and topknot, played the grey hawk.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a feast in the tower he set the actor Gao Guiqing to pour wine, made Zhixun play the military aide, and dressed Longyan in quail feathers and a topknot as the grey hawk.

sentences.zh: 知訓嘗使酒罵坐，語侵隆演，隆演愧恥涕泣，而知訓愈辱之。

translations.literal: Zhixun, drunk, cursed those seated and his words insulted Longyan; Longyan flushed with shame and wept, while Zhixun insulted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun, drunk, cursed the company and insulted Longyan to his face until the prince wept with shame—and Zhixun only heaped more abuse on him.

sentences.zh: 左右扶隆演起去，知訓殺吏一人，乃止。

translations.literal: Attendants helped Longyan rise and leave; Zhixun killed one clerk and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants helped Longyan away; Zhixun killed a servant and only then relented.

sentences.zh: 吳人皆仄目。

translations.literal: All the people of Wu looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu looked on in silent fury.

sentences.zh: 知訓又與朱瑾有隙，瑾已殺知訓，攜其首馳府中示隆演曰：「今日為吳除患矣。

translations.literal: Zhixun also had a rift with Zhu Jin. Jin had already killed Zhixun, carried his head galloping into the palace to show Longyan, and said: "Today I have removed a scourge for Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun had long been at odds with Zhu Jin. After killing him Jin rode into the palace with the head and told Longyan, "Today I have rid Wu of a plague."

sentences.zh: 」隆演曰：「此事非吾敢知。

translations.literal: " Longyan said: "This affair is not something I dare to know about."
translations.idiomatic: " Longyan said, "This is not for me to judge."

sentences.zh: 」遽起入內。

translations.literal: " He at once rose and went inside.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose at once and fled within.

sentences.zh: 瑾忿然，以首擊柱，提劍而出，府門已闔，逾垣，折其足，遂自刎死。

translations.literal: Jin flushed with anger, struck the pillar with the head, drew his sword and went out; the palace gate was already shut. He scaled the wall, broke his foot, and then cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jin in a fury smashed the head against a pillar, drew his sword, and strode out—but the gates were shut. He scaled the wall, broke his leg in the fall, and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 米誌誠聞瑾殺知訓，被甲率其家兵至天興門問瑾所在，聞瑾死，乃還。

translations.literal: Mi Zhicheng heard Jin had killed Zhixun, donned armor and led his household troops to the Tianxing Gate to ask where Jin was; hearing Jin was dead, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Zhicheng, hearing Jin had killed Zhixun, donned armor and led his household troops to the Tianxing Gate to find him; learning Jin was dead, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 徐溫疑誌誠助瑾，遣使殺之。

translations.literal: Xu Wen suspected Zhicheng had aided Jin and sent envoys to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen suspected Mi Zhicheng had aided Zhu Jin and sent men to kill him.

sentences.zh: 嚴可求懼事不克，使人偽從湖南境上來告軍捷，召諸將入賀，擒誌誠斬之。

translations.literal: Yan Keqiu feared the affair would fail; he had someone falsely report from the Hunan border that the army had won, summoned the generals in to congratulate, seized Zhicheng, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the plot would fail, Yan Keqiu staged a false report of victory from the Hunan frontier, summoned the generals to celebrate, seized Mi Zhicheng, and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 劉信克虔州，執譚全播以歸。

translations.literal: Liu Xin took Qianzhou and seized Tan Quanbo, bringing him back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin captured Qianzhou and brought Tan Quanbo back as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 溫之徙鎮金陵也，以其養子知誥守潤州。

translations.literal: When Wen moved his seat to Jinling, he left his adopted son Zhigao to guard Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen shifted his base to Jinling, he left his adopted son Xu Zhigao to hold Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 嚴可求嘗謂溫曰：「二郎君非徐氏子，而推賢下士，人望頗歸，若不去之，恐為後患。

translations.literal: Yan Keqiu once said to Wen: "The second young lord is no son of the Xu clan, yet he promotes the worthy and humbles himself before scholars; popular regard inclines to him. If he is not removed, I fear a later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Keqiu once warned Wen, "Zhigao is not a Xu by blood, yet he wins men by promoting talent and showing humility—if you do not remove him, he may become a threat."

sentences.zh: 」溫不能用其言。

translations.literal: " Wen could not adopt his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 及知誥秉政，其語泄，知誥出可求於楚州，可求懼，詣金陵見溫謀曰：「唐亡於今十二年，而吳猶不敢改天祐，可謂不負唐矣。

translations.literal: When Zhigao held government his words leaked out; Zhigao sent Keqiu out to Chuzhou. Keqiu was afraid and went to Jinling to see Wen, plotting: "Tang has been dead these twelve years, yet Wu still dares not change from Tianyou—this may be called not failing Tang."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigao took power the warning leaked; he posted Keqiu to Chuzhou. Keqiu fled to Jinling and told Wen, "Tang fell twelve years ago, yet Wu still dates its reign by Tianyou—that is loyalty enough to the old dynasty."

sentences.zh: 然吳所以征伐四方，而建基業者，常以興復為辭。

translations.literal: Yet the reason Wu campaigns on all sides and builds its foundation has always been the plea of restoring the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu has campaigned on every side and built its power always in the name of restoring Tang.

sentences.zh: 今聞河上之戰，梁兵屢絀，若李氏復興，其能屈節乎？

translations.literal: "Now I hear of the battles on the Yellow River—Liang troops repeatedly defeated. If the Li clan revives, can we bend our knees?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now Li Cunxu has destroyed Liang on the northern frontier. If Tang rises again, can we still bow as vassals?"

sentences.zh: 宜於此時先建國以自立。

translations.literal: "At this moment we ought first to establish a state and stand on our own."
translations.idiomatic: "This is the moment to proclaim a kingdom and stand on our own feet."

sentences.zh: 」溫深然之，因留可求不遣，方謀迫隆演僭號。

translations.literal: " Wen deeply agreed, kept Keqiu from being sent away, and began plotting to force Longyan to usurp the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen agreed wholeheartedly, kept Keqiu at his side, and began pressing Longyan to take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，隆演卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year Longyan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year Longyan died.

sentences.zh: 隆演少年嗣位，權在徐氏，及建國稱制，非其意，常怏怏，酣飲，稀復進食，遂至疾卒，年二十四，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: Longyan had succeeded young; power lay with the Xu clan. When a state was founded and he was made sovereign against his will, he was often discontent, drank deep, rarely ate again, and thus fell ill and died at twenty-four. His posthumous title was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Longyan had come to the throne young while the Xu clan held real power. Forced to preside over a kingdom he never wanted, he grew sullen, drank heavily, scarcely ate, and sickened and died at twenty-four; his posthumous title was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 弟溥立，僭號，追尊為高祖宣皇帝，陵曰肅陵。

translations.literal: His younger brother Pu succeeded, usurped the imperial title, and posthumously honored him as Emperor Xuan, the founding high ancestor, with the mausoleum Suling.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Pu succeeded him, declared himself emperor, and posthumously honored him as Emperor Xuan, founding ancestor of the line, with the mausoleum Suling.

sentences.zh: 溥，行密第四子也，隆演建國，封丹陽郡公。

translations.literal: Pu was Xingmi's fourth son. When Longyan founded the state, he was enfeoffed Duke of Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was Yang Xingmi's fourth son; when Longyan founded the kingdom he was made Duke of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 隆演卒，弟廬江公濛次當立，而徐氏秉政，不欲長君，乃立溥。

translations.literal: When Longyan died, his younger brother the Prince of Lujiang, Meng, was next to succeed, but the Xu clan held government and did not wish a mature ruler, so they enthroned Pu.
translations.idiomatic: When Longyan died his younger brother Meng, Prince of Lujiang, stood next in line, but the Xu clan preferred a pliable youth and enthroned Pu instead.

sentences.zh: 七月，改升州大都督府為金陵府，拜徐溫金陵尹。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the great metropolitan prefecture of Shengzhou was changed to Jinling Prefecture; Xu Wen was appointed Jinling Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Shengzhou's metropolitan prefecture became Jinling Prefecture, and Xu Wen was named its intendant.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，改元順義，赦境內。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year the era was changed to Shunyi and an amnesty was declared within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year the era became Shunyi and an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，祀天於南郊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter Heaven was worshipped at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter the court sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 禦天興樓，大赦。

translations.literal: He ascended the Tianxing Tower and proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the Tianxing Tower and proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 拜徐溫太師，嚴可求右僕射。

translations.literal: Xu Wen was appointed Grand Preceptor; Yan Keqiu, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen was made Grand Preceptor and Yan Keqiu Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，唐莊宗滅梁。

translations.literal: In the third year Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong destroyed Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang.

sentences.zh: 遣司農卿盧蘋使於唐，嚴可求密條數事授蘋以行。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of Agriculture Lu Ping as envoy to Tang; Yan Keqiu secretly listed several matters and entrusted them to Ping for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lu Ping, Minister of Agriculture, as envoy to Tang, with Yan Keqiu privately briefing him on several points to raise.

sentences.zh: 蘋見洛陽，莊宗問之，蘋次第以對，皆如所授。

translations.literal: Ping saw Zhuangzong at Luoyang; Zhuangzong questioned him and Ping answered in order, all as he had been instructed.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang Zhuangzong questioned him, and Ping answered point by point exactly as he had been coached.

sentences.zh: 四年，溥至白沙閱舟師，徐溫來見，以白沙為迎鑾鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Pu came to Baisha to review the fleet; Xu Wen came to meet him, and Baisha was made the Welcome-the-Imperial-Carriage garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Pu reviewed the fleet at Baisha; Xu Wen came to meet him, and Baisha was made the Welcome-the-Imperial-Carriage garrison.

sentences.zh: 五年，唐遣諫議大夫薛昭文使福州，假道江西，劉信出勞之，謂曰：「亞次聞有信否？

translations.literal: In the fifth year Tang sent Remonstrance Grandee Xue Zhaowen as envoy to Fuzhou, passing through Jiangxi. Liu Xin came out to entertain him and said: "Has Yaci heard of Xin?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Tang sent Xue Zhaowen, Remonstrance Grandee, to Fuzhou by way of Jiangxi. Liu Xin came out to greet him and asked, "Has the Son of Heaven heard of Liu Xin?"

sentences.zh: 」昭文曰：「天子新有河南，未熟公名也。

translations.literal: " Zhaowen said: "The Son of Heaven has newly taken Henan and is not yet familiar with your lordship's name."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaowen replied, "The Son of Heaven has only lately taken Henan and does not yet know your name."

sentences.zh: 」信曰：「漢有韓信，吳有劉信，君還，其語亞次，當來較射於淮上也。

translations.literal: " Xin said: "Han had Han Xin; Wu has Liu Xin. When you return, tell Yaci—he should come match archery on the Huai."
translations.idiomatic: " Xin said, "Han had Han Xin and Wu has Liu Xin. Tell the Son of Heaven when you return that I await him for an archery match on the Huai."

sentences.zh: 」乃酌大卮，望牙旗鎞首百步，謂昭文曰：「一發而中，願以此卮為壽，否則亦以自罰。

translations.literal: " He then poured a great goblet, looked a hundred paces toward the finial on the command pennant, and said to Zhaowen: "If one shot strikes true, I wish to offer this goblet in toast; if not, I shall punish myself with it as well."
translations.idiomatic: " He filled a great goblet, took aim at the finial on the command pennant a hundred paces off, and told Zhaowen, "If my first arrow strikes true, this cup is yours; if not, I drink it myself as penalty."

sentences.zh: 」言訖，而箭已穿矣。

translations.literal: " As he finished speaking, the arrow had already pierced through.
translations.idiomatic: " He had scarcely finished when the arrow drove through the target.

sentences.zh: 六年，追爵大丞相徐溫四代祖考，立廟於金陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the four generations of ancestors of Grand Chancellor Xu Wen were posthumously ennobled and a temple was established at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the court posthumously ennobled four generations of Xu Wen's ancestors and built a temple for them at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 左僕射徐知誥為侍中，右僕射嚴可求同平章事。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Xu Zhigao became Palace Attendant; Right Vice Director Yan Keqiu, Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao, Left Vice Director, became Palace Attendant; Yan Keqiu, Right Vice Director, became chancellor of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 是歲，莊宗崩，五月丁卯，詔為同光主輟朝七日。

translations.literal: That year Zhuangzong died; on the dingmao day of the fifth month an edict ordered court suspended for seven days for the late lord of Tongguang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhuangzong died; on the dingmao day of the fifth month the court suspended audiences for seven days of mourning.

sentences.zh: 七年，大丞相徐溫率吳文、武上表勸溥即皇帝位，溥未許而溫病卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Grand Chancellor Xu Wen led Wu civil and military officials in a memorial urging Pu to take the imperial throne. Pu had not yet agreed when Wen died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Grand Chancellor Xu Wen led the civil and military officials in urging Pu to take the imperial throne; Pu had not yet agreed when Wen fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚戌，溥禦文明殿即皇帝位，改元曰乾貞，大赦境內，追尊行密武皇帝，渥景皇帝，隆演宣皇帝。

translations.literal: On the gengxu day of the eleventh month Pu ascended the Civilization Hall and took the imperial throne, changed the era to Qianzhen, declared a great amnesty within the borders, and posthumously honored Xingmi as Emperor Wu, Wo as Emperor Jing, and Longyan as Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the eleventh month Pu took the throne in the Hall of Civilization, proclaimed the era Qianzhen, declared a great amnesty, and posthumously honored Xingmi as Emperor Wu, Wo as Emperor Jing, and Longyan as Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 以徐知誥為太尉兼侍中，拜溫子知詢輔國大將軍、金陵尹，治溫舊鎮。

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao was made Grand Marshal and Palace Attendant; Wen's son Zhixun was appointed Supporting-the-State Great General and Jinling Intendant, governing Wen's old seat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao was made Grand Marshal and Palace Attendant; Wen's son Zhixun was made Supporting-the-State Great General and Jinling intendant to hold Wen's old domain.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆封王。

translations.literal: All sons were enfeoffed as kings.
