translations.idiomatic: All his sons were enfeoffed as kings.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，封東海為廣德王，江瀆廣源王，淮瀆長源王，馬當上水府寧江王，采石中水府定江王，金山下水府鎮江王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the Eastern Sea was enfeoffed as King of Broad Virtue; the Jiang river spirit as King of Broad Source; the Huai river spirit as King of Long Source; the upper water office at Madian as King of Pacifying the Jiang; the middle water office at Caishi as King of Stabilizing the Jiang; the lower water office at Jinshan as King of Guarding the Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year the court enfeoffed the Eastern Sea as King of Broad Virtue, the Yangzi spirit as King of Broad Source, the Huai spirit as King of Long Source, and the upper, middle, and lower river regents at Madian, Caishi, and Jinshan as kings of the Jiang.

sentences.zh: 六月，荊南高季興來附，封季興秦王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Gao Jixing of Jingnan came to submit; Jixing was enfeoffed King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Gao Jixing of Jingnan submitted and was enfeoffed King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 九月，季興敗楚師於白田，獲其將吏三十四人來獻。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jixing defeated Chu troops at Baitian, captured thirty-four of their officers and clerks, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jixing defeated Chu forces at Baitian and sent thirty-four captured officers to the Wu court.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，金陵尹徐知詢來朝，知誥誣其有反狀，留之不遣，以為左統軍，斬其客將周廷望。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year Jinling Intendant Xu Zhixun came to court. Zhigao falsely accused him of rebellion, detained him and would not send him back, made him Left Commander-in-Chief, and beheaded his guest-general Zhou Tingwang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year Xu Zhixun, Jinling intendant, came to court; Zhigao accused him of treason, detained him, made him Left Commander-in-Chief in name only, and executed his officer Zhou Tingwang.

sentences.zh: 以徐知諤為金陵尹。

translations.literal: Xu Zhie was made Jinling Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhie was appointed Jinling intendant.

sentences.zh: 溥加尊號睿聖文明孝皇帝，大赦境內，改元大和，以徐知誥為中書令。

translations.literal: Pu added the honorific Emperor of Sagely Brilliance, Civilization, and Filial Piety, declared a great amnesty within the borders, changed the era to Dahe, and made Xu Zhigao Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pu took the honorific Emperor of Sagely Brilliance, Civilization, and Filial Piety, declared a great amnesty, changed the era to Dahe, and made Xu Zhigao Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，冊其子江都王璉為太子。

translations.literal: In the second year his son the Prince of Jiangdu, Lian, was invested as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year his son Lian, Prince of Jiangdu, was invested as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 三年，以徐知誥為金陵尹，以其子景通為司徒，及左僕射王令謀、右僕射宋齊丘皆平章事。

translations.literal: In the third year Xu Zhigao was made Jinling Intendant; his son Jingtong was made Minister of Education; and Left Vice Director Wang Lingmou and Right Vice Director Song Qiqiu were all Associate Directors of the Secretariat with the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xu Zhigao became Jinling intendant, his son Jingtong Minister of Education, and Wang Lingmou and Song Qiqiu, the Left and Right Vice Directors, all chancellors of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 四年，封知誥東海王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zhigao was enfeoffed King of the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhigao was enfeoffed King of the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 五年，建都於金陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the capital was established at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the capital was moved to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 六年閏正月，金陵火，罷建都，廢臨川王濛為歷陽公，知誥遣親信王宏以兵守之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the sixth year Jinling caught fire; the move of the capital was abandoned. The Prince of Linchuan, Meng, was demoted to Duke of Liyang; Zhigao sent his trusted man Wang Hong with troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of the sixth year fire swept Jinling and the move of the capital was abandoned; Meng, Prince of Linchuan, was demoted to Duke of Liyang and placed under guard by Zhigao's man Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 拜令謀司徒，宋齊丘司空。

translations.literal: Wang Lingmou was appointed Minister of Education; Song Qiqiu, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lingmou was made Minister of Education and Song Qiqiu Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 知誥召景通還金陵，為鎮海軍節度副使，以其子景遷為太保、平章事，與令謀等執政。

translations.literal: Zhigao summoned Jingtong back to Jinling as Deputy Military Governor of the Zhenhai Army, made his son Jingqian Grand Guardian and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Chancellery, and governed together with Lingmou and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao recalled Jingtong to Jinling as deputy military governor of the Zhenhai army, made his son Jingqian Grand Guardian and chancellor, and ruled with Lingmou and the rest.

sentences.zh: 七年九月，溥加尊號曰睿聖文明光孝應天弘道廣德皇帝，大赦，改元天祚。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year Pu added the honorific Emperor of Sagely Brilliance, Civilization, Filial Piety, Responding to Heaven, Expanding the Way, and Broad Virtue; declared a great amnesty and changed the era to Tianzuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the seventh year Pu took a still longer honorific title, declared a great amnesty, and changed the era to Tianzuo.

sentences.zh: 知誥進位太師、天下兵馬大元帥，封齊王。

translations.literal: Zhigao was advanced to Grand Preceptor and Great Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven and enfeoffed King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao was advanced to Grand Preceptor and supreme commander of all armies and enfeoffed King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 二年，景遷病，以次子景遂為門下侍郎、參政事。

translations.literal: In the second year Jingqian fell ill; his second son Jingsui was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Participant in Government.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Jingqian fell ill and his second son Jingsui was made Vice Director of the Secretariat with a seat in government.

sentences.zh: 三年，知誥建齊國，立宗廟、社稷，置左、右丞相已下，以金陵為西都，廣陵為東都。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhigao founded the state of Qi, established ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, appointed left and right chancellors and the ranks below, made Jinling the western capital and Guangling the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zhigao founded the state of Qi with its own temples and altars, appointed left and right chancellors, and made Jinling the western capital and Guangling the eastern.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，溥遣江夏王璘奉冊禪位於齊王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter Pu sent the Prince of Jiangxia, Lin, bearing the registers to yield the throne to the King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Pu sent Prince Lin of Jiangxia with the abdication registers to yield the throne to the King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，溥卒於丹陽，年三十八，謚曰睿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Pu died at Danyang at the age of thirty-eight. His posthumous title was Rui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Pu died at Danyang at the age of thirty-eight; his posthumous title was Rui.

sentences.zh: 升元六年，李遷其子孫於海陵，號永寧宮，嚴兵守之，絕不通人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shengyuan Li moved his descendants to Hailing in a place called the Palace of Everlasting Peace, guarded by strict troops with no contact permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shengyuan Li moved Yang Pu's descendants to Hailing in the Palace of Everlasting Peace, guarded so closely that no outsider might reach them.

sentences.zh: 久而男女自為匹偶，吳人多哀憐之。

translations.literal: After long years men and women paired among themselves; many people of Wu pitied them.
translations.idiomatic: In time the men and women paired among themselves, and the people of Wu looked on them with pity.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，世宗征淮南，下詔撫安楊氏子孫，而李景聞之，遣人盡殺其族。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande Emperor Shizong campaigned in Huainan and issued an edict to comfort and settle the Yang descendants; but Li Jing, hearing of it, sent men to kill the entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande, when Emperor Shizong of Zhou campaigned in Huainan and issued an edict to protect the Yang line, Li Jing of Southern Tang sent men to exterminate them all.

sentences.zh: 周先鋒都部署劉重進得其玉硯、馬腦碗、翡翠瓶以獻，楊氏遂絕。

translations.literal: Zhou's vanguard commander Liu Chongjin obtained their jade inkstone, agate bowl, and jadeite vase and presented them; the Yang line was thus extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chongjin, Zhou's vanguard commander, seized their jade inkstone, agate bowl, and jadeite vase as trophies—the house of Yang was ended.

sentences.zh: 徐溫，字敦美，海州朐山人也，少以販鹽為盜，行密起合淝，隸帳下。

translations.literal: Xu Wen, courtesy name Dunmei, was a native of Gushan in Haizhou. In youth he trafficked in salt as a bandit. When Xingmi rose at Hefei, Wen entered his service under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen, courtesy name Dunmei, came from Gushan in Haizhou. In youth he traded in salt and ran with bandits; when Yang Xingmi rose at Hefei, Wen joined his service.

sentences.zh: 行密所與起事劉威、陶雅之徒，號三十六英雄，獨溫未嘗有戰功。

translations.literal: Those who rose with Xingmi, such as Liu Wei and Tao Ya, were called the Thirty-Six Heroes; Wen alone had never won battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Those who rose with Xingmi—Liu Wei, Tao Ya, and the rest—were called the Thirty-Six Heroes; Wen alone had never won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 及行密欲殺朱延壽等，溫用其客嚴可求謀，教行密陽為目疾，事成，以功遷右衙指揮使，始預謀議。

translations.literal: When Xingmi wished to kill Zhu Yanshou and the others, Wen used the plan of his guest Yan Keqiu, teaching Xingmi to feign eye disease. When it succeeded, Wen was transferred for merit to Right Guards Commander and first joined in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi plotted to kill Zhu Yanshou and the rest, Wen turned to his adviser Yan Keqiu, who taught Xingmi to feign blindness. When the plot succeeded, Wen was made commander of the right guards and entered council for the first time.

sentences.zh: 及行密病，平生舊將，皆以戰守在外，而溫居帳下，遂預立渥之功。

translations.literal: When Xingmi fell ill, his old generals of a lifetime were all on campaign and garrison duty outside, while Wen remained in the headquarters tent and thus shared in the merit of enthroning Wo.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi fell ill, his veteran generals were all abroad on campaign while Wen stayed at headquarters and thus shared in placing Wo on the throne.

sentences.zh: 及弒渥，又與張顥有隙，使鐘章殺之。

translations.literal: After murdering Wo he again had a rift with Zhang Hao and had Zhong Zhang kill him.
translations.idiomatic: After murdering Wo he fell out with Zhang Hao and had Zhong Zhang kill him.

sentences.zh: 章許諾，選壯士三十人，椎牛享之，刺血為盟。

translations.literal: Zhang agreed, selected thirty stalwarts, slaughtered an ox to feast them, and pricked blood to seal the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang agreed, picked thirty stalwarts, slaughtered an ox for a feast, and sealed the pact in blood.

sentences.zh: 溫猶疑章不果，夜半使人探其意，陽謂曰：「溫有老母，懼事不成，不如且止。

translations.literal: Wen still doubted Zhang would act; at midnight he sent someone to probe his intent, who feigned saying: "Wen has an aged mother and fears the affair will fail—better to stop for now."
translations.idiomatic: Wen still doubted Zhang would act; at midnight he sent a man to test him, who pretended to say, "Wen has an aged mother and fears failure—better call it off."

sentences.zh: 」章曰：「言已出口，寧可已乎？

translations.literal: " Zhang said: "The words are already spoken—how can they be taken back?"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang said, "The words are spoken—there is no turning back."

sentences.zh: 」溫乃安。

translations.literal: " Wen was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen was reassured.

sentences.zh: 明日，鐘章殺顥，溫因盡殺紀祥等，歸弒渥之罪於顥，以其事入白渥母史氏。

translations.literal: The next day Zhong Zhang killed Hao. Wen then killed Ji Xiang and the others entirely, laid the crime of murdering Wo on Hao, and reported the matter to Wo's mother Lady Shi.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhang killed Hao; Wen then executed Ji Xiang and the rest, blamed Hao for Wo's murder, and reported the matter to Lady Shi, Wo's mother.

sentences.zh: 史悸而泣曰：「吾兒年幼，禍亂若此，得保百口以歸合淝，公之惠也。」

translations.literal: Shi trembled and wept: "My son was young; calamity and chaos like this—yet to preserve a hundred mouths and return to Hefei is your grace."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi wept and said, "My son was young, and chaos such as this—yet you have preserved our clan and brought us home to Hefei. That is your kindness."

sentences.zh: 隆演立，溫遂專政，遷升州刺史，治舟師於金陵。

translations.literal: When Longyan ascended, Wen then monopolized government, was transferred to Prefect of Shengzhou, and built a fleet at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When Longyan took the throne Wen seized real power, became prefect of Shengzhou, and built a fleet at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 大將李遇怒溫用事，出嫚言，溫使柴再用族遇於宣州。

translations.literal: The great general Li Yu, angered at Wen's hold on power, uttered insults; Wen had Chai Zaiyong exterminate Yu's clan at Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, a great general, cursed Wen's dominance; Wen sent Chai Zaiyong to wipe out his clan at Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密舊將，人人皆自疑，溫因偽下之，恭謹如見行密，諸將乃安。

translations.literal: Xingmi's old generals each grew suspicious of himself; Wen therefore feigned deference to them, courteous and respectful as if meeting Xingmi, and the generals were then reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi's old generals grew suspicious of one another; Wen treated them with feigned deference, as courteous as if Xingmi himself stood before them, and they were reassured.

sentences.zh: 八年，溫遷行軍司馬、潤州刺史、鎮海軍節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Wen was transferred to Acting Commander of the Campaign Army, Prefect of Runzhou, Military Governor of the Zhenhai Army, and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Wen became acting campaign commander, prefect of Runzhou, military governor of the Zhenhai army, and chancellor of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 十年，遣招討使李濤攻越，戰於臨安，裨將曹筠奔於越，濤敗被執。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he sent Suppression Commissioner Li Tao to attack Yue; they fought at Lin'an. Deputy general Cao Jun fled to Yue; Tao was defeated and captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he sent Li Tao against Yue; at Lin'an the deputy Cao Jun defected and Tao was captured.

sentences.zh: 溫間遣人語筠曰：「吾用汝為將，汝軍有求，吾不能給，是吾過也。

translations.literal: Wen secretly sent someone to tell Jun: "I employed you as a general; your army had requests I could not meet—that was my fault."
translations.idiomatic: Wen secretly sent word to Jun, "I made you a general and failed your men's requests—that was my fault."

sentences.zh: 」赦筠妻子不誅，厚遇之。

translations.literal: " He pardoned Jun's wife and children without execution and treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: " He spared Jun's wife and children and treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 秋，越人攻毗陵，溫戰於無錫，筠感溫前言，臨戰奔歸，遂敗越兵。

translations.literal: In autumn the Yue attacked Piling; Wen fought at Wuxi. Jun, moved by Wen's earlier words, fled back in the midst of battle and thus defeated Yue troops.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Yue attacked Piling; Wen met them at Wuxi. Moved by Wen's earlier mercy, Jun defected mid-battle and the Yue were routed.

sentences.zh: 十二年，封溫齊國公，兼兩浙招討使，始就鎮潤州，以升、潤、宣、常、池、黃六州為齊國。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Wen was enfeoffed Duke of Qi and concurrently Suppression Commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits; he first took his seat at Runzhou, with Sheng, Run, Xuan, Chang, Chi, and Huang—the six prefectures—as Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wen was made Duke of Qi and commissioner for the Two Zhe circuits, established his seat at Runzhou, and made Sheng, Run, Xuan, Chang, Chi, and Huang his Qi domain.

sentences.zh: 溫城升州，建大都督府。

translations.literal: Wen walled Shengzhou and built a great metropolitan prefectural headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wen fortified Shengzhou and built a metropolitan headquarters there.

sentences.zh: 十四年，徙治之，以其子知訓輔隆演於廣陵，而大事溫遙決之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he moved his administration there, left his son Zhixun to assist Longyan at Guangling, while great affairs Wen decided from afar.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he moved his seat there, left Zhixun to assist Longyan at Guangling, and decided great matters from afar.

sentences.zh: 知訓為朱瑾所殺，溫養子知誥自潤州先入，遂得政。

translations.literal: Zhixun was killed by Zhu Jin; Wen's adopted son Zhigao entered first from Runzhou and thus seized government.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Jin killed Zhixun, Wen's adopted son Zhigao marched in first from Runzhou and seized power.

sentences.zh: 溫雖奸詐多疑，而善用將吏。

translations.literal: Though Wen was treacherous and suspicious, he knew well how to use generals and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous and suspicious though he was, Wen knew how to use generals and officials.

sentences.zh: 江西劉信圍虔州，久不克，使人說譚全播出降，遣使報溫，溫怒曰：「信以十倍之眾，攻一城不下，而反用說客降之，何以威敵國？

translations.literal: Liu Xin of Jiangxi besieged Qianzhou long without taking it and sent men to persuade Tan Quanbo to surrender, then dispatched an envoy to report to Wen. Wen said in anger: "Xin with ten times the force cannot take one city, yet turns to persuaders to secure surrender—how can he awe enemy states?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin of Jiangxi besieged Qianzhou for months without success and sent envoys to coax Tan Quanbo into surrender. When Xin reported this to Wen, Wen raged, "With ten times the force you cannot take one city, yet you hire talkers to win surrender—how will that awe our enemies?"

sentences.zh: 」笞其使者而遣之，曰：「吾以笞信也。

translations.literal: " He flogged the envoy and sent him back, saying: "I flog him to flog Xin."
translations.idiomatic: " He had the envoy flogged and sent back, saying, "This lash is meant for Xin."

sentences.zh: 」因命濟師，遂破全播。

translations.literal: " He then ordered reinforcements and thus broke Quanbo.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered reinforcements and Quanbo was taken.

sentences.zh: 人有誣信逗留陰縱全播，言信將反者，信聞之，因自獻捷至金陵見溫，溫與信博，信斂骰子厲聲祝曰：「劉信欲背吳，願為惡彩，茍無二心，當成渾花。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Xin, saying he lingered and secretly let Quanbo go and that Xin would rebel. Xin heard of it and therefore came of his own accord with news of victory to Jinling to see Wen. Wen gambled with Xin; Xin gathered the dice and prayed in a harsh voice: "If Liu Xin wishes to betray Wu, may I throw an ill cast; if I have no second heart, may I throw a full red."
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Xin of stalling and secretly aiding Quanbo, saying he meant to rebel. Xin came to Jinling with news of victory and gambled with Wen. Gathering the dice he prayed aloud, "If I mean to betray Wu, let me throw ill; if my heart is loyal, let every die show red."

sentences.zh: 」溫遽止之，一擲，六子皆赤，溫慚，自以卮酒飲信，然終疑之。

translations.literal: " Wen hastily stopped him, but with one throw all six were red. Wen was ashamed and drank a goblet with Xin himself, yet in the end still doubted him.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen tried to stop him, but with one throw all six dice came up red. Ashamed, Wen shared a cup with him—yet he never quite trusted him again.

sentences.zh: 及唐師伐王衍，溫急召信至廣陵，以為左統軍，托以內備，遂奪其地。

translations.literal: When Tang troops campaigned against Wang Yan, Wen urgently summoned Xin to Guangling, made him Left Commander-in-Chief on the pretext of internal defense, and thus seized his territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang marched against Wang Yan, Wen summoned Xin to Guangling, made him Left Commander-in-Chief on the pretext of guarding the capital, and stripped him of his command in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 溫客尤見信者，惟駱知祥、嚴可求，可求善籌畫，知祥長於財利，溫嘗以軍旅問可求，國用問知祥，吳人謂之「嚴、駱。

translations.literal: Among Wen's guests the most trusted were Luo Zhixiang and Yan Keqiu; Keqiu excelled at planning, Zhixiang at finance. Wen would consult Keqiu on military affairs and Zhixiang on state revenue; the people of Wu called them "Yan and Luo."
translations.idiomatic: Of Wen's advisers the most trusted were Luo Zhixiang and Yan Keqiu—Keqiu for strategy, Zhixiang for revenue. Wu called them "Yan and Luo."

sentences.zh: 」溫亦自喜為智詐，尤得吳人之心。

translations.literal: " Wen also prided himself on cunning and especially won the hearts of the people of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen prided himself on his cunning and won the hearts of the Wu people as few rulers could.

sentences.zh: 初隨行密破趙锽，諸將皆爭取金帛，溫獨據余囷，作粥以食餓者。

translations.literal: When he first followed Xingmi in defeating Zhao Yin, the generals all scrambled for gold and silks; Wen alone seized the remaining granaries and made porridge to feed the starving.
translations.idiomatic: When he first followed Xingmi against Zhao Yin, the other generals seized gold and silk while Wen alone took the remaining grain and fed the starving with porridge.

sentences.zh: 十六年，溫請隆演即皇帝位，不許，又請即吳王位，乃許，遂建國改元，拜溫大丞相、都督中外諸軍事，封東海郡王。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Wen asked Longyan to take the imperial throne; it was not granted. He asked again for the kingship of Wu and it was granted; a state was founded and the era changed. Wen was appointed Grand Chancellor and Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad and enfeoffed King of Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Wen pressed Longyan to take the imperial title; refused, he won consent for the kingship of Wu instead. The kingdom was founded, the era changed, and Wen was made Grand Chancellor, commander of all armies, and King of the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 隆演卒，溫越次立其弟溥。

translations.literal: When Longyan died, Wen passed over the proper succession to enthrone his younger brother Pu.
translations.idiomatic: When Longyan died, Wen passed over the rightful heir to enthrone his younger brother Pu.

sentences.zh: 順義七年，溫又請溥即皇帝位，溥未許而溫病卒，年六十六，追封齊王，謚曰武。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shunyi Wen again asked Pu to take the imperial throne; Pu had not yet agreed when Wen died of illness at sixty-six. He was posthumously enfeoffed King of Qi with the posthumous title Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Shunyi Wen again urged Pu to take the imperial title; Pu had not yet agreed when Wen died at sixty-six. He was posthumously made King of Qi with the title Wu.

sentences.zh: 李僭號，號溫為義祖。

translations.literal: When Li usurped the imperial title, he styled Wen the Founding Ancestor of Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bian declared himself emperor, he honored Wen as the Founding Ancestor of Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，盜亦有道，信哉！

translations.literal: Alas—even among thieves there is a way; how true!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—even among thieves there is a way. How true that is!

sentences.zh: 行密之書，稱行密為人，寬仁雅信，能得士心。

translations.literal: In writings about Xingmi he is described as a man generous, humane, refined, and trustworthy, able to win the hearts of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The histories describe Xingmi as generous, humane, refined, and trustworthy—a man who could win men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 其將蔡儔叛於廬州，悉毀行密墳墓，及儔敗，而諸將皆請毀其墓以報之。

translations.literal: His general Cai Chou rebelled at Luzhou and utterly destroyed Xingmi's tombs. When Chou was defeated, the generals all asked to destroy his tomb in revenge.
translations.idiomatic: His general Cai Chou rebelled at Luzhou and desecrated Xingmi's tombs; when Chou was defeated the generals all demanded the same revenge on his grave.

sentences.zh: 行密嘆曰：「儔以此為惡，吾豈復為邪？

translations.literal: Xingmi sighed and said: "Chou did this as an evil deed—would I do the same?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sighed and said, "Chou did this out of malice—would I answer evil with evil?"

sentences.zh: 」嘗使從者張洪負劍而侍，洪拔劍擊行密，不中，洪死，復用洪所善陳紹負劍，不疑。

translations.literal: " He once had his attendant Zhang Hong carry a sword and attend him; Hong drew the sword and struck at Xingmi but missed; Hong died. He then again employed Chen Shao, whom Hong had favored, to carry the sword, without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: " Once he had his attendant Zhang Hong carry a sword at his side; Hong drew it and struck at Xingmi, missed, and was executed. Xingmi then appointed Chen Shao, whom Hong had favored, to carry the sword at his side without a second thought.

sentences.zh: 又嘗罵其將劉信，信忿，奔孫儒，行密戒左右勿追，曰：「信負我者邪？

translations.literal: He also once cursed his general Liu Xin; Xin in anger fled to Sun Ru. Xingmi warned those at his side not to pursue, saying: "Has Xin betrayed me?"
translations.idiomatic: He once cursed his general Liu Xin so harshly that Xin fled to Sun Ru in a rage. Xingmi told his men not to pursue and said, "Has Xin truly betrayed me?"

sentences.zh: 其醉而去，醒必復來。

translations.literal: He left in drunkenness; when sober he will surely return.
translations.idiomatic: He left in a drunken fit; when he sobers he will come back.

sentences.zh: 」明日，果來。

translations.literal: " The next day he did indeed come.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Xin returned as he had said.

sentences.zh: 行密起於盜賊，其下皆驍武雄暴，而樂為之用者，以此也。

translations.literal: Xingmi rose from banditry; those beneath him were all fierce, martial, and violent, yet glad to serve him—for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi had risen from banditry, and his followers were fierce, violent men—yet they served him gladly for reasons such as these.

sentences.zh: 故二世四主垂五十年。

translations.literal: Therefore two generations and four rulers endured for nearly fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: That is how two generations and four rulers held power for nearly fifty years.

sentences.zh: 及渥已下，政在徐溫。

translations.literal: From Wo downward, government lay with Xu Wen.
translations.idiomatic: From Wo onward real power rested with Xu Wen.

sentences.zh: 於此之時，天下大亂，中國之禍，篡弒相尋，而徐氏父子，區區詐力，裴回三主，不敢輕取之，何也？

translations.literal: At this time the realm was in great chaos; within China calamity followed calamity, usurpation and murder in succession. Yet the Xu father and son, with their petty deceitful force, hovered around three rulers and dared not lightly seize the throne—why?
translations.idiomatic: In those years the realm was torn apart, and across the heartland usurpation and murder followed one upon another. Yet the Xu father and son, for all their cunning, circled three puppet rulers for decades without daring to take the throne outright—why?

sentences.zh: 豈其恩威亦有在人者歟！

translations.literal: Was it not that their grace and awe also lay in the hearts of men!
translations.idiomatic: Surely it was because their kindness and their terror alike had taken root in men's hearts!
